response:
Thought for 33s

1. Will Sebastian actually use an Excel-tab kanban consistently?
No. It will fail within 2 weeks (probably sooner).

Failure modes (in order of likelihood):

Post-call admin fatigue: He finishes a call, has the next step in his head, but updating the Excel row feels like extra work. He skips it “for now” and never comes back.
Stale data death spiral: By day 4–5 the Pipeline tab no longer matches reality. He stops trusting it and stops using it.
No reminders = invisible next actions: “Seuraava toimenpide” is just text. He has to remember to open Excel and filter every morning. He won’t.
Context-switching tax: Phone call → hang up → open laptop → find row → filter → type → save. He will do it for the first 30 calls, then default to a notepad or email drafts.

Real-world pattern with solo reps: the simpler the tool looks on paper, the faster it becomes shelf-ware.

2. Is Excel-as-pipeline good enough for 1 rep + 20 accounts?
It is not.

Pipedrive (or any real pipeline tool) gives:

1-second drag-and-drop stage change
automatic activity logging
pop-up reminders
deal-age warnings
revenue forecast view

Excel gives none of that. For 20 accounts the volume is manageable, but the friction is lethal. Phone-first sales means Sebastian lives between calls. Every extra click between calls kills momentum. Excel is fundamentally broken here because it turns the pipeline into administrative homework instead of a live selling tool.

3. What is the MINIMUM viable pipeline that actually beats Pipedrive’s UX for this exact use case?
It can be built entirely inside the allowed stack (Excel + Obsidian + Python) and can be better than Pipedrive for a single phone-first rep with 20 accounts.

Minimum viable system (ready in <2 days):

Layer	Tool	What it does	Why it beats Pipedrive here
Source of truth	registry.xlsx (Asiakkaat + Pipeline tabs)	Master data + raw pipeline	Already exists
Daily cockpit	Python script (run once in morning)	Reads Pipeline tab → generates one Obsidian daily note with: today’s calls, overdue next actions, stalled deals, direct links to the 20 HTML briefs	Zero filtering. He opens one file every morning and sees exactly what to do.
Working memory	Obsidian (one note per top-20 company)	Call log, notes, linked HTML brief, Tasks plugin due dates	Native reminders + searchable history. Dataview query gives him a live kanban view inside Obsidian.
One-click logging	Simple Python GUI or even just a template	“Log call” form that appends timestamp + outcome + next step directly into Excel and into the Obsidian note	Faster than Pipedrive’s activity log for this scale.

This is dramatically less friction than Pipedrive for 20 accounts and zero SaaS cost.

4. What does Sebastian need on his very first call that a Pipedrive user would have but our current system doesn’t give him?

Instant, one-click access to the company’s full history (even if it’s just “never contacted”).
Pre-filled next-step suggestion and due date.
One-click way to log outcome + set next action without leaving the call flow.
Visual cue if the deal is getting old (Pipedrive shows deal age in red).

Right now he has the HTML brief (excellent) but zero integration. After the call he has to hunt for the row in Excel. That gap is exactly where deals die.

5. Verdict: Is the current registry.xlsx + HTML briefs system good enough to pass the April 25 kill switch?
No. It is not.

It is a classic “looks fine on paper, fails in real life” design. With only 18 working days, a new rep, and zero buffer, the manual Excel kanban will become stale by April 15 and Sebastian will be flying blind. The HTML briefs are a strong asset, but the pipeline tracking is the weak link that will kill the project.

Fix it in the next 48 hours with the Obsidian + Python layer described in #3.
That version gives Sebastian a system he will actually use every single day and gives leadership a clean, auditable pipeline to evaluate on April 25. The current version does not.

The design is broken as-is. Fix it or the kill switch will be pulled.
